theater: 斯巴達、歐羅塔斯河谷與伊托墨山

battle.name: 前464年斯巴達地震
battle.theater: 斯巴達、歐羅塔斯河谷與伊托墨山
battle.brief: 公元前464年冬春之交，強震擊中拉科尼亞的斯巴達城，屋舍倒塌、神廟傾毀，市民退守島上；斯巴達隨即要求雅典出兵鎮壓，一場由天災引發的希洛人與美塞尼亞人起義就此爆發，戰事延燒至伊托墨山。卡面的科林斯青銅盔正是斯巴達重裝步兵的世代裝備：地動之後，正是靠它與盾牆維持秩序。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries: 這場戰爭的奇特之處在於，交戰雙方並非對等的國家：一邊是拉科尼亞的斯巴達城邦，另一邊是斯巴達自己的奴屬——美塞尼亞人與拉科尼亞的希洛人；起義爆發之後又有一批外部城邦被拉進來，使它成了一場內亂與城邦之戰混雜在一起的戰爭。斯巴達一方以公民兵為骨幹：成年男性公民按共膳班編伍，平時受嚴格的集體教養，戰時以重裝步兵列陣；國家權力由兩支王族分掌，國王之下設五名監察官與長老會議；外圍則是庇里奧基人與伯羅奔尼撒聯盟的盟邦。震後第一個前來援助的是科林斯人，據狄奧多羅斯記載，趕到斯巴達一邊的是科林斯與其他若干盟邦；阿卡迪亞同盟與斯巴達保持同盟，沒有加入起義。另一邊是占據伊托墨山的起義軍：美塞尼亞人熟悉梅塞尼亞與拉科尼亞的山地與道路，希洛人則是熟悉農地和村莊分布的農業人口，兩者合流，使斯巴達人在自己的本土反而處處陌生。外來援助來自阿爾戈斯與伊利斯，這兩座城與斯巴達的宿怨最深，阿爾戈斯其後更在美塞尼亞重新建城一事上扮演了關鍵角色。最曲折的一層是雅典：斯巴達向雅典求援，雅典派出重裝步兵協助鎮壓；事隔不久，雅典卻轉而與美塞尼亞人、阿爾戈斯人站在一起，把斯巴達拖進一個對手的聯盟裡。
countriesEn: What makes this war odd is that the two sides were not equal states: on one side stood the city-state of Sparta in Laconia, on the other Sparta's own unfree population, the Messenians and the helots of Laconia; and once the revolt had begun a number of outside cities were pulled into it, so that what followed was a civil war and a war between states mixed together. The Spartan side was built on the citizen levy: men of military age were organized into messes, passed through a severe collective upbringing in time of peace, and fought in battle as hoplites; state power was shared between two royal houses, with five ephors and a council of elders below the kings; outside them stood the perioikoi and the allied cities of the Peloponnesian League. The first ally to send help was Corinth; Diodorus records that the Corinthians were among the first to arrive on the Spartan side, together with a number of other allied cities, while the Arcadian League kept its alliance with Sparta and did not join the revolt. On the other side stood the insurgents holding Mount Ithome: the Messenians knew the mountains and roads of Messenia and Laconia intimately, and the helots, being agricultural populations, knew the distribution of the farms and villages, so that the Spartans found themselves on unfamiliar ground in their own country. Outside aid came from Argos and Elis, the two cities with the deepest grudge against Sparta, and Argos was later to play a decisive part in the refounding of Messene. The most tangled layer is Athens: Sparta called on Athens for help, and Athens sent hoplites to help put the revolt down; not long afterwards, however, Athens turned to stand with the Messenians and the Argives, and drew Sparta into a coalition of its enemies.
people: 留下姓名的關鍵人物分屬三處。斯巴達方面，兩支王族之一的國王阿納克桑德羅斯在與起義軍的交鋒中受傷，狄奧多羅斯記下了這一條；監察官才是真正主持應戰的人，震後正是他們決定讓外邦人入城、決定撤守島上、也決定收編外邦部隊。美塞尼亞人方面，傳說中的領袖是阿里斯托美涅斯：保桑尼德說他出身於埃普提托斯一族的後裔，第一次梅塞尼亞戰爭之後流散多年，於是聚集舊部與逃亡者，在伊托墨山修築堡壘抵抗，據說堅持了三十三年；這段記載帶有明顯的史詩色彩，現代學者多不願逐字採信，但阿里斯托美涅斯這個人物確實在後世的梅塞尼亞民族記憶中長期存在。雅典方面是基蒙，米太亞德之子，年輕時已與斯巴達有往來；修昔底德記載斯巴達向雅典求援後，雅典派出二百名重裝步兵由他率領前往拉科尼亞，這是他第一次獨力統兵，後來他才在波斯戰線上揚名。留下記錄的人還有：修昔底德在《伯羅奔尼撒戰爭史》第一卷留下最早也最簡的記載；狄奧多羅斯《歷史文庫》第十一卷最為詳細，記下地震、盟邦援軍，以及那場讓斯巴達國王受傷的敗仗；斯特拉波《地理學》第八卷記述地震造成的破壞與斯巴達人的應變，並記下一則監察官作答的軼事；保桑尼德《梅塞尼亞書》提供起義者視角，亞里士多德《政治學》則提供制度變化的線索；還有以《斯巴達地震頌歌》留名的詩人阿里斯托德莫斯，傳世僅存殘篇。
peopleEn: Those whose names survive belong to three places. On the Spartan side, Anaxander, king of one of the two royal houses, was wounded in the fighting against the insurgents, and Diodorus records the fact; the ephors were the men who actually directed the response, and it was they who decided after the earthquake to let foreigners into the city, to withdraw to the island, and to take foreign troops into service. On the Messenian side the legendary leader is Aristomenes: Pausanias says that he was a descendant of the line of Aepytus, that he wandered for many years after the First Messenian War, and that he then gathered the survivors and the fugitives, built a fortress on Mount Ithome and held out, according to the story, for thirty-three years; the account carries a strong epic colouring and modern scholars are unwilling to take it literally, but the figure of Aristomenes did endure for a long time in the Messenian memory of the nation. On the Athenian side was Cimon, the son of Miltiades, who already had connections with Sparta while still young; Thucydides records that after Sparta called on Athens, the city sent two hundred hoplites under his command to Laconia, which was his first independent command, long before he made his name on the Persian front. Those who left the record include: Thucydides, whose first book of the History of the Peloponnesian War holds the earliest and the shortest account; Diodorus Siculus, whose eleventh book of the Library of History is the fullest, giving the earthquake, the allied contingents, and the defeat in which the Spartan king was wounded; Strabo, whose eighth book of the Geography describes the destruction and the Spartan response, and preserves a quip of the ephors; Pausanias, whose Messenian book supplies the insurgents' side of the story, and Aristotle, whose Politics supplies the thread of institutional change; and Aristodemus, the poet whose paean on the Spartan earthquake survives only in fragments.
kits: 卡面這頂科林斯青銅盔屬於重裝步兵的前一代裝備，這一點必須先說清楚：公元前464年，標準的希臘重裝步兵早已改戴前五世紀初定型、視野開闊的阿提卡式青銅盔；全正面封閉、只留一條眼鼻狹縫的科林斯式面甲已退居次要，只在保守隊伍、儀仗與古物收藏中留蹤。科林斯式盔約重一公斤上下，戴上之後只能靠隊形與聲音行動，這正是卡面那句「看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活」的來處。回到這場戰爭：斯巴達公民步兵的裝備核心是阿爾戈斯式大圓盾、約兩公尺半的長矛（荷馬所稱的「阿伽墨儂矛」）、短劍與銅製脛甲；美塞尼亞人與希洛人的武備則以農具改製的矛、投槍與少量盾為主，披甲者比例低得多，這也是起義軍屢次在正面會戰中被壓垮的原因。攻城方面，這場戰爭幾乎沒有機械可用：當時尚無成形的投石機與撞槌，圍伊托墨山靠的是合圍牆、封鎖補給與掘地逼近；保桑尼德記載掘進者被對方反挖的坑道與積水所困，圍城者幾乎全靠人力與封鎖線撐住。真正決定震後秩序的不是任何一件兵器，而是盾牆能否重新結起、列隊能否重新排成，以及城防重建的速度。
kitsEn: The Corinthian bronze helmet on the card belongs to the previous generation of hoplite equipment, and that has to be said plainly first: by 464 BC the standard Greek hoplite had long since taken to the open-faced Attic bronze helmet, which was fixed in type in the early fifth century BC; the fully closed Corinthian type, with the eyes and nose shut in behind a narrow slit, had already been pushed into the background, surviving only in conservative units, in ceremonial display and in old collections. The Corinthian helmet runs to about a kilogram, and once it is on, the wearer can act only by formation and by hearing, which is where the card's line comes from: the visible price is that the man who wears it can live only through the formation. Back to this war: the core of the Spartan citizen soldier's equipment was the Argive-type great round shield, a spear of about two and a half metres, the short sword and bronze greaves, the spear being the long one Homer calls the spear of Agamemnon; the Messenians and helots, by contrast, fought with spears and javelins made over from farm tools and with a bare handful of shields, and the proportion of armoured men among them was far lower, which is why the insurgents were repeatedly crushed in open battle. As for siege work, this war had almost no machinery: there were no developed stone-throwers and no battering rams to hand, and the investment of Mount Ithome rested on a circumvallation wall, on cutting off supplies and on digging toward the defenders; Pausanias records that the miners were trapped by counter-mines and by the water, so that the besiegers were held up almost entirely by men and by the line of blockade. What really decided the order after the earthquake was not any single weapon, but whether the shield wall could be closed again, whether the line could be re-formed, and how fast the defences could be rebuilt.
tactics: 這場戰爭的戰術可以拆成三段。第一段是天災造成的戰術性癱瘓：地震把斯巴達的街道、屋舍與神廟同時掀翻，市民與守軍在廢墟中斷了數日，斯巴達一度撤守對岸的島嶼；城市秩序一散，重裝步兵的盾牆就無從結起，凡是沒有地方重新排成縱隊的地面，就等於沒有軍隊。第二段是起義軍的戰術：以伊托墨山為核心的堡壘式抵抗。起義軍不求在平原上與重裝步兵決戰，而是利用山地、峽道與對地形的熟悉，一再襲擊斯巴達的封鎖線與徵召線；斯巴達的反應是標準的希臘圍城邏輯——合圍牆、封鎖補給、掘地逼近，屢次攻上山頂卻屢次被反擊下來。第三段是正面會戰的細節，也是整場戰爭反覆出現的一組對照：起義軍一旦離開山地進入開闊地，便被斯巴達的縱隊壓垮；反過來，斯巴達的縱隊一旦離開開闊地進入丘陵，就會被切斷退路並失去盾牆的相互掩護。公元前462年前後，雅典人與阿爾戈斯人加入美塞尼亞人一側之後，會戰的天平第一次明顯傾斜，狄奧多羅斯記下的那場敗仗、斯巴達國王阿納克桑德羅斯受傷，即由此而起。最後是政治上的戰術：斯巴達震後打破數百年不許外邦人入城的規矩，准許雅典兵進城駐守，這在戰術上是應急之舉，在制度上卻是史無前例的破例。
tacticsEn: The tactics of this war can be taken apart into three parts. The first is the tactical paralysis caused by the disaster: the earthquake overturned the streets, the houses and the temples of Sparta at once, the citizens and the garrison were cut off among the ruins for several days, and Sparta withdrew for a time to the island across the water. Once the order of the city dissolved, the shield wall of the hoplites could not be closed, and any ground on which a line could not be re-formed was in effect no army at all. The second is the tactic of the insurgents: a resistance built round the fortress of Mount Ithome. They did not seek a decision with the hoplites in the open plain; they used the mountains, the passes and their intimate knowledge of the ground to raid the Spartan blockade and the lines on which men were called up. The Spartan answer was the standard Greek logic of siege: a circumvallation wall, a cut against supplies, and digging toward the defenders; they reached the top of the hill again and again and were thrown back again and again. The third is the detail of the pitched battle, and it is also the contrast that runs through the whole war: the moment the insurgents left the hills for open ground they were crushed by the Spartan column, and conversely the Spartan column, once it left open ground for broken country, was cut off from its line of retreat and lost the mutual cover of the shield wall. Around 462 BC, when Athenians and Argives joined the Messenian side, the balance of the pitched battle tipped visibly for the first time, and it was in that defeat which Diodorus records that the Spartan king Anaxander was wounded. Last comes the political tactic: after the earthquake Sparta broke the rule of centuries that kept foreigners out of the city and allowed Athenian troops to quarter inside it, an act that was an expedient in tactical terms and a breach without precedent in institutional terms.
data: 可核的數字大致如下。時間：地震與起義通行紀年為公元前464年，古籍未記確切月份；起義的主戰期多繫於公元前464至前459年，個別學者把它延長到前460年。兵力：修昔底德記載雅典應斯巴達之請派出二百名重裝步兵，由基蒙率領，這是全篇最硬的一條數字；狄奧多羅斯記斯巴達一方的盟邦援軍以科林斯人為先，阿爾戈斯與伊利斯站在起義軍一方；保桑尼德記斯巴達曾派四千名希洛人到阿卡迪亞的帕爾忒尼翁建立殖民地，這批人隨即叛離斯巴達加入起義軍。守備：起義軍在伊托墨山修築堡壘，保桑尼德記阿里斯托美涅斯率眾抵抗三十三年，這是傳說數字，學界多視為不可逐字採信。距離：伊托墨山距斯巴達城直線不足二十公里，是拉科尼亞與梅塞尼亞交界處的山地要塞。震級：現代地質學者依史料描述推估在六點五至七級之間，但這是現代推定，並非當時記載。傷亡：關於起義雙方的損失，古籍幾乎完全沉默，可確認的只有國王阿納克桑德羅斯受傷、斯巴達在與雅典及美塞尼亞聯軍的會戰中失利，以及公元前459年伊托墨守軍被准許撤走並以金錢贖取自由。結算：公元前446/5年的「三十年和平」由雅典、科林斯、麥加羅波利斯與美塞尼亞人分別簽字，確認美塞尼亞的自治；前426/5年雅典把部分美塞尼亞人安置在瑙帕克托斯；其後亦有移民遷往西西里，參與建立占巴，今日墨西拿之名即由此而來。
dataEn: The checkable figures run roughly as follows. Date: the earthquake and the revolt are conventionally dated to 464 BC, and the ancient sources give no month; the main fighting is usually placed between 464 and 459 BC, with some scholars extending it to 460 BC. Numbers on the field: Thucydides records that Athens, in answer to Sparta's call, sent two hundred hoplites under Cimon, and that is the hardest figure in the whole story; Diodorus records that the allied reinforcements for Sparta came from Corinth first, and that Argos and Elis stood on the insurgents' side; Pausanias records that Sparta sent four thousand helots to establish a colony at Parthenion in Arcadia, and that these at once deserted Sparta and joined the revolt. Defences: the insurgents built a fortress on Mount Ithome, and Pausanias records Aristomenes leading the resistance there for thirty-three years, a legendary figure which scholars generally decline to take literally. Distance: Mount Ithome lies less than twenty kilometres in a straight line from the city of Sparta, a mountain stronghold on the boundary between Laconia and Messenia. Magnitude: modern geologists infer from the descriptions in the sources a figure between six and a half and seven on the modern scale, but that is a modern inference and not a record of the time. Losses: on the casualties of both sides the ancient sources are very nearly silent, and what can be confirmed is that the king Anaxander was wounded, that Sparta lost a pitched battle to the Athenians and Messenians, and that in 459 BC the garrison of Ithome was allowed to withdraw and bought its freedom with money. Settlement: the Thirty Years' Peace of 446/5 BC was signed separately by Athens, Corinth, Megalopolis and the Messenians and confirmed Messenian autonomy; in 426/5 BC Athens settled a part of the Messenians at Naupactus; and later some emigrants moved to Sicily and took part in the foundation of Zancle, from which the modern name of Messina comes.
cause: 直接起因就是一場地震，但地震只是把早已存在的裂痕震開。斯巴達的國家基礎是對希洛人的控制：梅塞尼亞在公元前八世紀被征服，全境人口淪為國有奴隸，斯巴達公民則靠這批人的勞動養活，國家的一切榮光都建立在这套制度上。這套制度天生不穩，靠的是兩根柱子——五名監察官的嚴苛監督，以及城邦對外封閉、外邦人不得入城的傳統；柱子一斷，制度便失去彈性。公元前480年之後的二十餘年裡，斯巴達表面上是希臘頭號城邦，內裡卻出現多處預警：公民人口長期不增、戰損無從補充、國王權威被監察官逐步架空；希洛人口在城邦腹地日增，一旦有外來援助到來，造反就不難。震後斯巴達向雅典求援這件事本身就說明問題：封閉政策已經無法承受外來兵力，也就無法在地震之後迅速恢復秩序。希洛人不會放過這個窗口，賴以維持的開墾與牧放計劃在震後無從運作，城外莊園與葡萄園是壓力最直接的地方。傳統上還把地震視為神罰：保桑尼德說這是對斯巴達奴役美塞尼亞人的懲罰，阿爾斯托德莫斯的頌歌也把地震寫成天譴；阿里斯托美涅斯的形象之所以能流傳，正因為敘事把起義寫成一次正義的清算。當然也要提醒：所謂斯巴達少年在奧林匹克場上公開羞辱伊利斯優勝者利西馬庫斯的那則軼事，據說正出現在這前後十年間，它說明的是社會風氣在鬆動，而不是制度已經崩潰。
causeEn: The direct cause was an earthquake, but the earthquake only shook open a fracture that had been there long before. The foundation of the Spartan state was control of the helots: Messenia was conquered in the eighth century BC, its whole population was reduced to state-owned slaves, the Spartan citizens lived off the labour of that population, and every distinction the state enjoyed rested on the system. The system was inherently unstable, and it rested on two pillars: the harsh supervision of the five ephors, and the tradition that the city stayed closed and admitted no foreigners. Once a pillar broke, the system lost its elasticity. In the two decades or so after 480 BC, Sparta looked like the leading city of Greece while inwardly showing warning signs in several places: the citizen population did not grow, battle losses could not be replaced, and the authority of the kings was hollowed out step by step by the ephors; the helot population grew inside the territory of the city, and once outside help arrived, revolt was not difficult. The fact that Sparta turned to Athens for help after the quake says enough by itself: the closed-city policy could no longer bear foreign troops, and therefore could not restore order quickly after the earthquake. The helots would not let the window close; the ploughing and pasturage on which the arrangement rested could no longer be carried on, and the farms and vineyards outside the walls were where the pressure was most direct. Tradition also reads the earthquake as a punishment from the gods: Pausanias says it was the penalty for Sparta's enslavement of the Messenians, and the paean of Aristodemus writes the earthquake as divine vengeance; the figure of Aristomenes endured precisely because the narrative cast the revolt as a righteous reckoning. It should be added, however, that the well-known anecdote of Spartan youths openly insulting the Olympic victor Lysimachus of Elis is said to belong to the ten years around this time, and what it shows is that the manners of the society were loosening, not that the institutions had already collapsed.
impact: 最深遠的影響是斯巴達國家形態的永久改變，三件事同時發生。第一件是對外封閉的結束：震後斯巴達准許雅典兵進城、准許外邦部隊留駐，這在五世紀之前的斯巴達是沒有的先例，遠方城邦的援兵從此可以在城內出入；往後的斯巴達再也沒有真正關過門。第二件是制度層面的重整：狄奧多羅斯與亞里士多德都提到地震之後斯巴達以「三十人」一類的機構整飭法律與王政，監察官權力在震後進一步坐實，長老會的組成與選拔方式被重新規定；學界一般把監察官制度的成形放在六世紀末至前五世紀初，但把它的運作調整繫於這場危機，是有史料支持的。與此同時，斯巴達在五世紀中葉建起城牆——在希臘城邦中這極不尋常，雅典的城牆要到前478/7年才築，城市的加固往往意味著對自身防衛的重新評估。第三件是希洛體制的變形：美塞尼亞實際獲得自治，前446/5年「三十年和平」予以確認，前369/8年底比斯的埃帕米農達斯更在梅塞尼亞建城，把這份自治固定成城邦。對外部世界而言，這場震動也改變了希臘的權力地圖：斯巴達與阿爾戈斯的宿怨從此升級為兵戎相見，雅典與美塞尼亞人及阿爾戈斯的聯盟在修昔底德筆下成為壓在斯巴達頭上的三邊鉗制。希臘人從此認定，斯巴達的強大建立在一個隨時可能裂開的奴隸制之上；這種判斷在後來對斯巴達霸權的每一次挑戰中都被反覆引用。
impactEn: The deepest effect was a permanent change in the shape of the Spartan state, and three things happened at once. The first was the end of the closed city: after the quake Sparta allowed Athenian troops inside the walls and foreign contingents to stay, a thing without precedent in Sparta before the fifth century, and from then on the reinforcements of distant cities could move about inside the city; the Sparta of later years never truly shut its gates again. The second was a reform at the level of institutions: Diodorus and Aristotle both record that after the earthquake Sparta set up a body of thirty to put the laws and the kingship in order, the power of the ephors was further entrenched after the quake, and the composition and the selection of the council of elders were redefined; scholars generally place the formation of the ephorate in the late sixth and early fifth centuries BC, but tying the adjustment of its working to this crisis is supported by the sources. At the same time Sparta built city walls in the middle of the fifth century, which was highly unusual among the Greek city-states, since the walls of Athens were not begun until 478/7 BC; the fortification of a town usually marks a fresh assessment of its own defence. The third was the reshaping of the helot system: Messenia in practice won autonomy, confirmed by the Thirty Years' Peace of 446/5 BC, and in 369/8 BC Epaminondas of Thebes founded a city in Messenia and fixed that autonomy as a polis. For the world outside, the shock also rearranged the map of Greek power: the old feud between Sparta and Argos hardened into open war, and the alliance of Athens with the Messenians and the Argives became, in Thucydides' account, a three-sided pincer pressing on Sparta. From then on the Greeks held that the strength of Sparta rested on a system of slavery that might split open at any moment; that judgement was cited again and again in every later challenge to Spartan hegemony.
result: 就戰爭本身而言，公元前464年的地震所引發的這場起義，最後以斯巴達一方的鎮壓成功告終：起義軍退守伊托墨山，圍城拖了數年，斯巴達以錢財買下守軍的自由，公元前459年守軍得以撤走，美塞尼亞人各奔前程。往後數十年裡，這批流散者構成一股有組織的政治力量：前446/5年他們作為簽約方得到自治的承認，前426/5年一部分人隨雅典人遷往瑙帕克托斯，前369/8年埃帕米農達斯在梅塞尼亞建城，把他們重新編為公民，昔日的起義者終於取得城邦身分。對斯巴達而言，代價則是實實在在的：公民兵與盟邦兵的折損、四年多的戰事開支、外邦人入城的制度破例、無法再靠封閉政策維持的威信；希洛人口仍在境內，但控制成本更高，國家的擴張能力自此大不如前，這正是它在十餘年後無法重建霸權的一個原因。回頭看這場戰爭的結局，最耐人尋味的一點是：地震只毀了斯巴達的建築，卻讓被壓在建築下面的結構浮出水面——希洛體制、外邦禁令與公民人口三者的互相支撐，第一次被地震和起義同時撕開，斯巴達此後再也沒有把它們縫回原樣。
resultEn: As a war, the revolt provoked by the earthquake of 464 BC ended in a success for the suppression: the insurgents withdrew to Mount Ithome, the siege dragged on for years, Sparta bought the freedom of the garrison with money, in 459 BC the defenders were allowed to leave, and the Messenians scattered to wherever they could. Over the following decades those exiles formed an organized political force: in 446/5 BC they were a signatory party to a settlement that confirmed their autonomy, in 426/5 BC a part of them moved to Naupactus with the Athenians, and in 369/8 BC Epaminondas founded a city in Messenia and enrolled them once more as citizens, so that the rebels of old at last gained the standing of a polis. For Sparta the price was plain and present: the loss of citizen and allied soldiers, the cost of more than four years of war, the breach of the rule against foreigners in the city, and a prestige that could no longer be kept up by the old policy of closure. The helot population was still inside the territory, but the cost of controlling them was higher, and the capacity of the state to expand was much weaker from then on, which is one reason why it could not rebuild its hegemony a dozen years later. Looking back at the outcome, the most telling point is this: the earthquake destroyed only the buildings of Sparta, but it brought to the surface the structure that had been held down beneath them. The mutual support of the helot system, the ban on foreigners and the size of the citizen body was torn open for the first time by earthquake and revolt together, and Sparta never managed to stitch it back together as it had been.
